newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says tourism up despite hostage crisis.
newsitem.headline: Peru says tourism up despite hostage crisis.

text.p: The government said Wednesday the number of tourists visiting Peru since the Dec. 17 takeover of the Japanese ambassador's residence by Marxist rebels had risen by 13.56 percent compared with the previous year.
A statement from government promotions' body PromPeru said 55,641 tourists had entered Peru between Dec. 17 and the end of January, up from 48,999 in the same period of the previous year.

"Even if there was uncertainty at first, as the days went by, it began to be understood internationally that the events at the Japanese ambassador's residence are an isolated case that does not affect the security of visitors," the statement said. "The situation is beginning to normalize and there are no more cancellations."
More than 600,000 tourists visited Peru in 1996, up from 485,000 the previous year.

Although traditionally popular for its archaeological riches, Inca ruins and dramatic Andean and jungle scenery, Peru lost favor with tourists following the outbreak of a violent guerrilla war in 1980.
But since the diminishment of guerrilla violence since 1992, the tourism industry has been recovering fast.
